extracted.intended_audience: patent prosecutors, patent attorneys/agents, and in-house counsel drafting U.S. utility patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting U.S. patent specifications and claims with Post-Grant (PTAB/PGR/IPR/reexamination) proceedings and later amendment/reissue strategies in mind. Emphasizes specification content, claim structure, prosecution choices, and evidentiary record-building to survive or respond to post-grant challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting with IPR/PTAB in mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter Partes Review at the PTAB is the dominant patent invalidity venue; patents are challenged under 102 and 103 using printed publications. PTAB applies broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI) for unexpired patents, which can yield claim constructions narrower than district courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate that a petitioner will use prior art printed publications and that claim construction at PTAB will often be broader (BRI) relative to district court. Draft claims and spec to withstand these challenges by clarifying terms and providing fallback claim sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a detailed specification to anchor construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB defers to clear spec definitions; a claim term defined in the spec is construed accordingly even under BRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed descriptions and definitions in the spec for critical terms (express lexicography) so the PTAB will construe claim terms consistent with those definitions. Provide examples and embodiments that illustrate intended meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express lexicography for critical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use express lexicography for critical terms so that a claim term defined in the spec is construed accordingly by the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly define key claim terms in the specification and, where appropriate, explain scope and alternatives. Avoid ambiguity in term usage and provide clear anchors that can be relied upon during post-grant review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on claim differentiation at the PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim differentiation is a less powerful tool at the PTAB; do not rely on it to broaden one claim by reference to a narrower one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because PTAB gives limited weight to claim differentiation, draft independent and dependent claims so each stands on its own; provide explicit support in the spec for any broader interpretations rather than depending on differentiation arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multiple independent claims of varying scope
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner challenges only some claims, the unchallenged claims survive even if the challenged ones do not. Multiple independent claims of varying scope create more pieces that can survive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft a graduated set of independent claims (broad and narrower independent claims) to increase chances that some claims remain if others are cancelled. Consider claim sets that capture different aspects/variants of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disparaging statements in spec or prosecution history
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything in the spec or prosecution history that disparages an alternative approach can be quoted by the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay neutral in describing alternatives and prior approaches. Avoid language that disparages other methods or embodiments, since such statements can be used as admissions or evidence of exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long, detailed specification to support amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A long, detailed spec provides anchors for amendments at the PTAB. The PTAB allows amendments only with full spec support; sparse specs limit amendment options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft comprehensive disclosures and multiple embodiments so that, if amendment is needed in post-grant proceedings, there is clear basis in the spec to add or modify claim language. Provide various fallback examples and explicit linking language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand Post-Grant Review (PGR) timing and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: PGR is broader than IPR (any ground of invalidity, not just 102/103) but only available within 9 months of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the 9-month PGR window following grant and that PGR permits challenges on a wider set of grounds. Consider prosecution and filing timing to manage exposure during that window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know Ex Parte Reexamination characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: EPR (Ex Parte Reexamination) is less common but available; ex parte means the patentee handles examination directly with the examiner and the petitioner has no further role after triggering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ex parte reexamination as a potential path for correcting validity issues where appropriate, knowing third parties have limited ongoing participation once reexamination is instituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue options and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee can file a reissue to broaden or narrow claims within 2 years of issuance (broadening) or any time (narrowing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider timely reissue applications if post-grant analysis shows scope errors. Use reissue to correct claim scope, remembering the 2-year limit for broadening reissues and the differing availability for narrowing reissues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution choice: broad claims plus narrow backups
rubrics_metrics.description: If only broad claims issue, an IPR challenge that succeeds wipes out the patent. If a graduated claim ladder issued, narrow backups survive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance pursuing broad claims with issuing narrower dependent or independent backups. Where appropriate, pursue a ladder of claims so that narrower claims persist even if broader claims are cancelled in post-grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argue economically during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Every argument made during prosecution can be cited at the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive or unnecessary argumentation that narrows claim scope or creates admissions. Make only necessary, strategic arguments and preserve flexibility for post-grant defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: File continuations prior to IPR filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Once IPR is filed, the patentee's options for amendment are limited. Pending continuations allow new claims to be drafted to capture the accused product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain pending continuations before an IPR is filed so you can pursue additional claim drafting and protect embodiments/products that might otherwise be lost. Use continuations strategically as part of an overall portfolio defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document secondary considerations/evidence during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Document secondary considerations: commercial success, long-felt need, copying, industry praise. Build the file during prosecution and keep records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and maintain contemporaneous evidence of commercial success, copying by others, industry praise, and long-felt need to support non-obviousness in later proceedings. Ensure such evidence is properly dated and preserved in prosecution files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate high institution and claim-cancellation rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern IPR institution rates are roughly 60%, with ~80% of instituted petitions resulting in cancellation of at least some claims. Drafting must anticipate this challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt drafting and prosecution strategies (detailed spec, claim ladders, continuations, careful argumentation, evidence collection) that assume a realistic chance of post-grant challenge and partial cancellation.
